articles.title: The long end has stopped listening to the data
articles.summary: US payrolls missed badly and the 10-year Treasury still closed higher. Benchmark yields are at the highs of the year in every major market while credit spreads have hardly moved. That is not a contradiction. The forces lifting long yields are not credit forces.

articles.title: Japan at the Turn: the outlook for inflation, growth, unemployment and interest rates
articles.summary: Japan has not escaped its debt problem; it has changed the currency in which that problem is paid. The adjustment is running through the exchange rate and the price level, not the bond market. Executive summary; full paper available to clients.

articles.title: Taylor Rule sensitivity analysis: United States and Australia
articles.summary: Sensitivity matrices for the rule-implied policy rate under a range of neutral-rate and inflation assumptions. On current core PCE the rule sits 100–200bp above the funds rate; in Australia a positive output gap validates the cash rate at a modest trimmed-mean assumption.

articles.title: Kevin Warsh: a background paper on his monetary theory and policy views
articles.summary: Career, intellectual influences and record of the 17th Chair of the Federal Reserve. Less a doctrinaire hawk than a market-oriented pragmatist: fewer signals, a higher bar for balance-sheet intervention, closer attention to asset prices.

articles.title: The Hormuz shock: commodity price transmission, drivers and curve-implied outlook
articles.homeTitle: The Hormuz shock: commodity price transmission and curve-implied outlook
articles.summary: Oil and urea, priced on liquid forward curves, have round-tripped. Sulphur and helium, with no curve, kept rising after the strait reopened. Why market structure, not just physical exposure, sets how a commodity prices a geopolitical shock.
